newsitem.title: USA: Tribune set to close Renaissance buy Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Tribune set to close Renaissance buy Tuesday.

text.p: Tribune Co, which won conditional regulatory approval Monday to acquire Renaissance Communications Corp, said Tuesday it expected to close the $1.13 billion transaction sometime during the day.
The Renaissance purchase would make Tribune the second-largest television station owner in the United States, with 17 outlets reaching about 33 percent of U.S. homes with televisions.
"The (Federal Communications Commission) action allows the deal to close, and we expect it to close today," a Tribune spokeswoman told Reuters on Tuesday.

The FCC granted a 12-month waiver of a rule against cross-ownership of television stations and newspapers in the same market. The rule would have required the company to sell either WDZL-TV in Miami or its Sun-Sentinel newspaper in nearby Ft. Lauderdale, Florida, in order to complete the deal.

"We're confident we can keep both properties as the FCC reviews its cross-ownership rules in 1998," the spokeswoman said. "The company has a strategy and the structure in place to keep both," she said.

A spokesman for the FCC confirmed that the agency next year was scheduled to review all of its broadcast policies, including television-newspaper cross-ownership rules, though there was no indication so far that any current policies would be changed.

The FCC order regarding Renaissance rejected the Tribune's request for a permanent exemption in favor of the 12-month waiver, allowing for the orderly sale of either the Miami station or the Ft. Lauderdale newspaper.
Tribune shares were up 3/8 at 41-1/4 in early afternoon trading on Tuesday.
